title: Large Language Models as Optimizers
abstract: This paper proposes Optimization by PROmpting (OPRO), a simple and effective approach to leverage large language models (LLMs) as optimizers. OPRO uses LLMs to generate new solutions based on the optimization problem description and previously evaluated solutions. We demonstrate the potential of OPRO on linear regression, traveling salesman problems, and prompt optimization, outperforming human-designed prompts by up to 8% on GSM8K and 50% on Big-Bench Hard tasks.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a complex math problem. You can use a large language model to generate solutions based on the problem description and previous attempts. This is the core idea behind Optimization by PROmpting (OPRO). By leveraging the power of LLMs, we can simplify the optimization process and achieve impressive results.

OPRO works by using LLMs to generate new solutions, which are then evaluated and added to the optimization process. This creates a feedback loop that helps the LLM improve its solutions over time.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
The OPRO framework consists of three main components: the optimizer LLM, the scorer LLM, and the meta-prompt. The optimizer LLM generates new solutions based on the meta-prompt, which contains the problem description, previous solutions, and their scores. The scorer LLM evaluates the new solutions and provides feedback to the optimizer LLM.

This process is repeated until convergence, resulting in a high-quality solution to the optimization problem.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
We evaluated OPRO on several benchmarks, including GSM8K and Big-Bench Hard. Our results show that OPRO outperforms human-designed prompts by up to 8% on GSM8K and 50% on Big-Bench Hard tasks.

The following chart shows the performance of OPRO on GSM8K, with an average accuracy of 80.2% compared to 71.8% for human-designed prompts.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
OPRO has significant implications for optimization problems in various fields, including math, computer science, and operations research. By leveraging the power of LLMs, we can simplify the optimization process and achieve impressive results.

OPRO also has the potential to transfer knowledge across different domains and tasks, enabling the development of more generalizable and robust optimization methods.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
The key innovations of OPRO include the use of LLMs as optimizers and the design of the meta-prompt. The meta-prompt contains the problem description, previous solutions, and their scores, enabling the LLM to generate new solutions based on the optimization trajectory.

OPRO also introduces a feedback loop that helps the LLM improve its solutions over time, resulting in a high-quality solution to the optimization problem.
